_Good day Mr Xu,_ 

_I'm truly sorry, your mails arrived in my SPAMs (should be corrected now), and I wasn't in copy from the last mail (where new revison has been resubmitted), so I only can answer now._ 

_The anchor point correspond exactly to the geometrical corner of the container you select. For your current case below, it corresponds to the Door (let's say it door side) Left Bottom corner for Tier 1. Every dx, dy and dz will be added to correct the position of this point._ 

_Thus, since only this point can be displaced, and since the stowage point is attached to an other exact geometrical corner on Vertical Lashing, both distances of those points (anchor and stowage) to the theoritical geometrical corners they are attached to, need to be added at the anchor point (as it is the only point which can me moved). So the displacement is more or less fictive at anchor point, but allow to have the correct angle and length for the bar, which is what matters in the computations. That's why we have this 89 mm correction to be added for dy at the bottom for instance, since in reality the stowage point isn't attached to the exact corner, but 89mm next to the corner, at the opening within the corner casting._ 

_For your example : I've corrected below in_ **_red_** _your values for dy and dz example in your previous mail._ 

_I've just began otherwise review of your new resubmission. So far everything is good for the CSA part, I've just those new comments :_ 

_- Unrestricted case : For 40' case on deck BAY 14;22 : only 5 tier are drawn for row 13-14, whereas 6 mass are displayed. We considered it was a mistake and that 6 containers were to be displayed row 13-14. If not, row 11-12 will not pass due to wind forces on top container and vertical forces ratio of 1,09. In any case, please clarify and update._

_- Unrestricted case 40' and 40'HC : cetner of gravity of the stacks is 20cm aft the 0.65L (where L rule length). Please, for the case for 0.65L, select and ohter bay for 40' and 40'HC in hold and on deck (between bay 02 and 10)._

_- Unrestricted case : For 40'HC case on deck BAY 34 Row 09-10 ; computed sum of the mass is 93MT, whereas it is indicated 100MT. Please clarify and correct accordingly._ 

_- For WW case 40' case on deck, BAY Row 08, we considered as per drawing that 40' stack was totally uncovered and unprotected from wind by external 20' row BAY 03. If it was to be protected, then your initial stowage in revision 0 of 20MT by container was allowed and didn't need to be updated, but in this case, it would have to be clearly indicated on the drawing. But current case in your new revision is good also. So let us know._ 

_For other stacks. All the ratios are below 1 and don't need to be updated neither on deck, nor in the hold._ 

_For the Veristar Lashing version, I'll try to put you in touch with someone in BV China who should enable you to get adaptated version. (Version I used was 3.6.2)._ 

_If it still doesn't work, let me know and I'll send you other screenshots (I enclosed you already the ones for BAY 30 Row14), but it's not very optimal to understand I guess... Also as I said, all your stacks are now passing._ 

_I hope also my explanation helped you to better understand our methodology._ 

_Let me know if it's still not clear and/or if you don't manage to get new version of the software._ 

_Best regards,_ 

_Cédric AUBERT_

_- For 20' bays on deck, END position is checked correctly for all bays, but not GAP position (I only noticed few of them). All bays should be also checked for their GAP positions where the only twistlocks are midlocks BD-2K (SWL 250/210, vertical gap 20mm, horizontal gap 5mm), as per CSM. You can only represent some on those bays if representaitve enough (accelerations increase the furthest the bay is from center line CL)._

_- y position not exactly correct for the bottom aft left corner of your stacks. Impact should however be very low, it's not critical. If you want ot correct anyway, for BAY 02-34, y positions for ROW 02, 04, 06, 08, 10, 12 and 14 are respectively 60mm, 2523mm, 5121mm, 7584mm, 10047mm, 12510mm and 14973mm, and for BAY 38 13mm, 2476mm, 4939mm, 7402mm, 9865mm, 12423mm and 14886mm._ 

_- BAY 37-39 and BAY 38 Row10, For Standard (8'6'' high) containers, only 84.8% of the bottom container surface is exposed whereas 15.2% of the second top container (Tier 7 for 20' stacks) is also exposed (nad not 100% and 0% respectively as per you file), since difference in bottom postion of the stacks between Row 10 and 12 isn't equal to exactly 8'6'', so second top container partially exposed. This increases the moment of force due to wind and can increase vertical forces up to 2-3% on the most critical cornpost. You'll find some examples of corrections for the 40' stacks in attached document. Please update, impact is strong._

_-  Breakwater sutrcuture is provided and can be ticked in Basic ship data (will reduce longitudinal loads, but impact very low, not critical)._

_- Intermediate plate value in basic ship data to be changed from 0mm to 30mm (correct thickness of intermediate twsitlocks). It impacts lashing bar geometries (vertical length Lz), height of stacks and accelerations (because of slightly higher stacks). It is critical and can increase also vertical loads up to 2% on some examples, both for 20' and 40' stowages.  Please update, impact is strong._

_- z bottom value BAY 38 Row 14 sin't 19.837mm, but 19.778mm (impact should be negligible)._

_- Incorrect positionning for vertical rods :  y value should be 0mm, and not 89mm, since openings within the corner casting and and within the lashing padeye are perfectly alligned.  Please update, impact is strong._

_- More generally, it seems there is a misunderstanding on the use of VeriSTAR Lashing to compute  correct lashing geometries (it is indeed not very explicit in the software and drawings in VeriSTAR Lashing can be sometimes misleading). Two major points need to be updated :_

_==> 89mm to be removed from your horizontal values on VeriSTAR Lashing. Indeed, veristar lashing doesn't remove by itself the 89mm corresponding to the distance between the corner of the container and the center of the coner casting. So you have to modify your dy value manually. When bar is lashed on padeye on external side of the container (external side being the furthest from the center line) and the top end on the internal side of the container, so for a stack on port side, when padeye is on port side, (and generally dy is negative for a stack on Port side (caution however, it can also be positive, but in general negative)), you have to remove those 89mm. In the opposite case, you ahe to add those 89mm. Caution also, correction for vertical rods is different (dy should be 0 for all those rods on this ship). You'll find some examples of corrections for the 40' stacks in attached document.  Please update, impact is strong._

_==> 118mm to be added to dz value for all the bars lashed to the top of a container (so in this case for all bays lashed to Tier 1), so to take into account the distance between top of container and bottom of corner casting (see BV methodology where reference point for a bar lashed to a top corner casting is bottom of this corner casting). You'll find some examples of corrections for the 40' stacks in attached document. Please update, impact is strong._

_I haven't checked all the geometries, but I didn't find other issues (if they are according to your pdf document for lashing geometries it should be fine)._ 

_At the end, the Info Length bar helps you to check the final length of the bar, to see if it's consistant and if they is no mistake in dx, dy or dz value._ 

_Please note that you made some approximations on dx and dz values which won't be critical, but note that then trying to reach exactly the maximum ratio of 1.00 for allowable forces is taking the risk that stack doesn't pass in our computations sometimes for 1 or 2kN. But normaly, with all the corrections in red, you should find the same results as we did (with and error margin of 1 or 2kN, I expect)._ 

_Otherwise, I don't see any other mistake and all the other parameters are correctly inputed._ 

_For your pdf document, some approximations were made on dx and dz values, but for those few milimeters, I don't expect any noticible impact on the results. So your PDF document of lashing geometry is perfectly fine._

_If anything isn't clear, please do not hesitate to contact me._ 

_Best regards,_ 

_Cédric AUBERT_
